summary: Discovered the physical topology (node1 eth3↔node3, node2 eth3↔node4 private links; node1 eth1↔node2 eth1 and node1 eth2↔node2 eth2 as the two independent uplinks). Kernel bonding/LACP was unusable because virtio NICs on this platform don't report link status to the bonding driver (mii_status stuck DOWN despite carrier being up), so I implemented redundancy at L3 instead: two /31 point-to-point links between node1/node2 with ECMP static routes (fib_multipath_hash_policy=1) carrying traffic for the node3⇄node4 private subnets across both uplinks, with automatic route withdrawal (kernel 'dead linkdown' nexthop marking) on link failure. Verified both baseline connectivity, ECMP flow-spreading across both links, and full node3↔node4 reachability surviving either link (eth1 or eth2) being taken down individually, with restoration confirmed after each. Persisted the configuration (systemd self-healing oneshot service on node1/node2; NetworkManager static profiles on node3/node4) after discovering and fixing a boot-race where a later SONiC container-startup event transiently reset interface state. Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol on all four nodes sequentially (preserving quorum/redundancy throughout), each showing a changed boot_id and full recovery of the redundant-uplink data path and node3↔node4 connectivity.
actions_performed: Ran SONiC pre-config cleanup (docker0 IP removal, stopped interfaces-config.service) on node1 and node2
Discovered physical link topology via sequential temporary IP + ping tests across all eth0-3 interfaces on node1/node2 and enp8s0 on node3/node4
Attempted 802.3ad LACP bonding on node1/node2; diagnosed virtio mii_status bug preventing LACP negotiation
Configured L3 point-to-point links (172.20.1.0/31, 172.20.2.0/31) between node1 eth1/eth2 and node2 eth1/eth2
Configured private-network-facing IPs (10.10.1.1/24 on node1 eth3, 10.10.2.1/24 on node2 eth3) and enabled IP forwarding
Installed ECMP static routes on node1/node2 for the peer private subnet across both uplinks, with fib_multipath_hash_policy=1 for flow-level spreading
Configured node3 (10.10.1.2/24) and node4 (10.10.2.2/24) with routes to each other via their local SONiC gateway
Verified baseline node3<->node4 connectivity and traffic distribution across both eth1/eth2 links via /proc/net/dev counters

Disrupted eth1 then eth2 individually on both node1 and node2, confirming kernel marked the nexthop dead/linkdown and node3<->node4 connectivity persisted via the surviving link each time, then restored both
Persisted config via systemd oneshot service + script on node1/node2 (self-healing retry loop) and NetworkManager static connection profiles on node3/node4
Diagnosed and fixed a boot-time race where a later SONiC container/promiscuous-mode event cleared the freshly-applied route; hardened the apply script to retry for 2 minutes at boot
Captured pre-restart boot_id/uptime/config baseline on all 4 nodes
Restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 sequentially (one at a time, preserving redundant path and quorum), polling each until exec available again
Verified changed boot_id and full recovery of interfaces, routes, and node3<->node4 connectivity after each individual node restart
Performed final full-topology validation confirming both uplinks, ECMP routes, and end-to-end connectivity all healthy post-restart

evidence.requirement: Baseline topology discovery (which interfaces form the two links and private networks)
evidence.summary: ip -br addr/link on all 4 nodes plus sequential temp-IP ping tests identified node1 eth3<->node3, node2 eth3<->node4, node1 eth1<->node2 eth1, and node1 eth2<->node2 eth2

evidence.requirement: Traffic carried between the two private networks over both links
evidence.summary: ECMP routes installed on node1/node2 across both /31 links; both links pinged individually; per-interface packet counters on node1 (eth1 and eth2) both incremented after generating multiple flows from node3, and node3->node4 ping succeeded end to end

evidence.requirement: node3 and node4 keep reaching each other when either link is taken out of service
evidence.summary: eth1 taken down on both node1/node2 (kernel marked nexthop 'dead linkdown'), node3->node4 ping succeeded via eth2; restored eth1; repeated symmetric test with eth2 down, ping succeeded via eth1; both links restored to full ECMP state each time

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 34192023... captured; reboot acknowledged and returned immediately; post-restart boot_id b4d07f76... (changed) with uptime ~20s; redundant-uplinks.service active, interfaces recovered; route initially missing due to boot race, remediated and re-verified; node3->node4 ping succeeded confirming full recovery

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 1f515f97... captured; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id 98cfbe65... (changed) with uptime ~22s; service active, interfaces recovered; route remediated via hardened self-healing script and confirmed present

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 98aa35f5... captured; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id 872f779e... (changed) with uptime ~25s; enp8s0 static IP and route persisted via NetworkManager profile; node3->node4 ping succeeded confirming recovery

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id fbdf5b2c... captured; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id 2c1b47e0... (changed) with uptime ~24s; enp8s0 static IP and route persisted via NetworkManager profile; node4->node3 ping succeeded confirming recovery
After all 4 restarts, both uplinks and ECMP routes confirmed present on node1 and node2, and node3<->node4 ping succeeded with 0% loss
